findings.title: Z.AI quota response with an out-of-range unit/number crashes the app (Int(Double) trap), and the crash repeats from the disk cache
findings.source: Response body of GET https://api.z.ai/api/monitor/usage/quota/limit (ZAIProvider.swift:50, http.fetchPayload), decoded in ZAIProvider.decodeSnapshot (ZAIProvider.swift:58)
findings.sink: Sources/AiTaskbarProviders/ZAIWireTypes.swift:83 and :84, where Int($0) converts a Double that was never checked for range
findings.description: flexibleDoubleIfPresent (AppConfig.swift:199-203) accepts any finite JSON number as a Double, and the code passes it straight to Int(_:) with no range or isFinite check. In Swift, Int(Double) is a runtime trap when the value does not fit in Int (above about 9.22e18), so this is a crash rather than a thrown error. The decode happens in decodeSnapshot, which is not protected by the do/catch around it, because a trap cannot be caught.
findings.exploit_scenario: The Z.AI endpoint, or anything that can shape its JSON, returns {"code":200,"success":true,"data":{"limits":[{"type":"TOKENS_LIMIT","unit":1e19,"number":1}]}}. ZAILimitEntry.init calls Int(1e19) and the process aborts. CachedFetch saves the raw payload in the DiskCache, so every later cache or stale-fallback decode aborts again, until the cache is cleared or overwritten by a clean fetch.
preconditions: attacker controls or influences the Z.AI API response (the threat model given)
findings.impact: Denial of service for the menu-bar app (crash, possibly a crash loop while the poisoned cache entry lasts). No confidentiality or integrity impact.
findings.fix: Convert with Int(exactly:) after rounding, or check range first, and return nil when the value is out of range, for example flexibleDoubleIfPresent(...).flatMap { $0.isFinite ? Int(exactly: $0.rounded()) : nil }. Consider a shared flexibleIntIfPresent helper in Core that decodes Int64 first and uses an exact conversion as the fallback.
findings.evidence: ZAIWireTypes.swift:83-84 `.map { Int($0) }` on the result of flexibleDoubleIfPresent, and AppConfig.swift:200 `try? decodeIfPresent(Double.self…)` accepts values like 1e19. There is no other place where unit or number are checked before this conversion.
